path: limits where Python refuses the size
pattern: above 500 mm Rust gives the ISO 286 limits, Python refuses the size
evidence: The maintainer's decision Q8 (docs/questions.md, 2026-10-09): extend ISO 286 to 3150 mm in both engines. The oracle was captured from specify-core cc341dd, whose standards.py (identical to main c1694ec) stops at 500 mm; the Python extension (branch iso286-3150 of specify-core) did not exist when this was captured. Rust's values are ISO 286-1:2010 Table 1 (IT5-IT11), Table 2 (f, g, h) and Table 3 (k, m, n, p) for 500-3150 mm, cross-checked against ISO 286-2 limits for g6, h6, k6, m6, f7 in every range (tests/standards.rs, fit_limits_match_iso_286_to_3150_mm). Every row up to 500 mm is equal. This path is given only where Python's own message is its size refusal and the size is at most 3150 mm (tests/standards.rs, iso286_equals_pythons); an unequal pair of limits is path 'limits', which no entry matches. Regenerate tests/fixtures/iso286_oracle.json.gz from that branch when it lands (see iso286_oracle.py): these entries then go stale.
